newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Fruit of Loom chief fights for job.
newsitem.headline: Irish Fruit of Loom chief fights for job.

text.p: The managing director of Fruit of the Loom's Irish businesses, Willie McCarter, has appealed to Dublin's High Court for an injunction against a redundancy notice served on him by his American bosses, court officials said on Thursday.

McCarter, his sales director brother John and finance director Seamus McEleney applied to the High Court on Wednesday for injunctions against the redundancy notices which were served on them in May. The case will be heard in two weeks' time, the officials said.
The Irish media speculated that the move to remove the three executives was linked to a dispute with the management of the European arm of Fruit of the Loom.
McCarter and colleagues were believed to be unhappy about the high overheads and losses being accumulated by the European wing, media reports said.
Nobody was available for comment at Fruit of the Loom.

The textile group, one of Ireland's largest manufacturing employers with between 3,000 and 3,500 workers at seven plants, has the distinction of having businesses on both sides of the Northern Ireland border.
McCarter, who is chairman of the International Fund for Ireland, has been a major figure in Irish business and very active in promoting cross-border relations.

Earlier this year former U.S. senator George Mitchell asked Willie McCarter to stay on for another term as chairman of the International Fund for Ireland, a body committed to financing industry in the border counties.

In 1986, the U.S. Fruit of the Loom bought McCarter's Ireland interests in Derry and Donegal from the McCarter family and Willie McCarter was appointed managing director of the Irish operations in 1987.
The current dispute appears to have been growing since the beginning of the year when some of McCarter's responsibilities were transferred back to the U.S., media reports said.

The Irish Independent newspaper said files at the Company Records office show that Fruit of the Loom in Ireland slid into the red with a pre-tax loss of 13.5 million pounds sterling ($21.4 million) in 1995, down from a profit of 5.8 million in 1994.
Market sources say the parent company wants to restructure its operation in Europe and that is one of the reasons for serving redundancy notices. ($ = 0.630 British Pounds Sterling)
